feed.title: Databases — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Awesome DB Tools
entry.summary: A list of tools that make working with databases easier (clients, migration, schema). Unlike single-database lists it looks at engine-agnostic helper tools.

entry.title: Awesome MongoDB
entry.summary: A list of libraries and tools for MongoDB, the document-based NoSQL database. Unlike general NoSQL lists it focuses on one product’s driver and ODM ecosystem.

entry.title: Awesome Postgres
entry.summary: A list of extensions, tools and resources for PostgreSQL. Unlike the official docs it shows the ecosystem’s extensions and management tools together.

entry.title: CockroachDB
entry.summary: A distributed SQL database that scales horizontally with strong consistency and survivability.

entry.title: dbdiagram.io
entry.summary: A tool that turns a simple text DSL into shareable ER diagrams fast.

entry.title: DBeaver
entry.summary: A universal desktop database client managing many databases from one interface.

entry.title: MariaDB
entry.summary: A community-driven open-source fork of MySQL, usable as a drop-in replacement.

entry.title: Modern SQL
entry.summary: A resource teaching modern SQL features such as window functions across dialects.

entry.title: Neon
entry.summary: Serverless Postgres with branching and scale-to-zero, spinning up instant database branches.

entry.title: PlanetScale
entry.summary: Serverless MySQL built on Vitess, managing schema changes with a branching workflow.

entry.title: PostgreSQL Exercises
entry.summary: Practise SQL with graded PostgreSQL exercises in the browser.

entry.title: SQLBolt
entry.summary: Interactive SQL lessons that teach by doing in the browser.

entry.title: SurrealDB
entry.summary: A multi-model database combining document, graph and relational in one engine.

entry.title: Use The Index, Luke!
entry.summary: The go-to developer-focused guide to SQL indexing and performance.

entry.title: Turso
entry.summary: A database platform built on libSQL, a SQLite fork, that replicates the database to edge nodes near the user. Unlike centralised services such as PlanetScale, read latency becomes local file access rather than a network round trip.

entry.title: Oracle SQL Developer
entry.summary: A free desktop client for Oracle databases combining querying, schema browsing and PL/SQL debugging — the de facto tool if you work with Oracle.

entry.title: PocketBase
entry.summary: A backend shipping as one Go file, providing SQLite, auth and a real-time API. Unlike heavy stacks it reduces the server to a single executable.

entry.title: SQLite
entry.summary: A serverless embedded database living in a single file — the most widely deployed database engine in the world, with a copy inside nearly every app on your phone. Its test coverage is legendary.

entry.title: SQLZoo
entry.summary: An exercise set that teaches SQL by making you write queries in the browser, each section over its own dataset. That is the difference from tutorials needing an install: your first `SELECT` requires no database.

entry.title: Supabase
entry.summary: An open-source Firebase alternative adding auth, APIs and storage on top of Postgres. Unlike Firebase it stands on relational Postgres and can be self-hosted.

entry.title: SQL Nasıl Öğrenilir
entry.summary: A thread where experienced users argue over how to learn SQL. Because nobody there is selling a course, the filtering is already done.

entry.title: Couchbase Learn
entry.summary: Queries a document store with a SQL-like language (N1QL), which is a gentler break for teams arriving from the relational world than MongoDB’s query syntax.

entry.title: Firebase
entry.summary: Realtime database, auth, storage and hosting in one package. It accelerates a prototype sharply, while query flexibility and vendor lock-in become the later problem.

entry.title: MongoDB University
entry.summary: MongoDB’s official free courses. The data modelling unit is the important one — designing a document store with relational habits is the most common source of performance trouble.

entry.title: MySQL Tutorial
entry.summary: Works MySQL end to end over a sample database, treating join types, subqueries and stored procedures separately. Far more readable as an introduction than the official manual.

entry.title: PostgreSQL Tutorial
entry.summary: A PostgreSQL tutorial showing each topic with a runnable query, going deep on window functions and CTEs where most SQL courses stop.

entry.title: İlişkisel Veritabanı Tasarımı
entry.summary: A full course on normal forms and schema design. It teaches getting the tables right rather than writing queries — which is where every later problem originates.

entry.title: Veritabanları Derinlemesine
entry.summary: A course on internals — index structures, transaction isolation levels, locking. Not a product tutorial; it holds regardless of which database you use.

entry.title: SQL Sıfırdan İleri Seviye
entry.summary: SQL from basics to advanced in four hours for anyone who wants the whole picture in one sitting. It reaches window functions rather than stopping at basic SELECT.
